# Quayside

The look of this project, generated from its tokens file. Agents read it, with the generated CSS, before any UI work.

## Overview

A, settlement statement. Batches of invoices read like a bank settlement statement: a neutral ground, one blue for actions and links, amounts in a monospace face so columns align.

Sources: fixture: no reference capture.

## Motion

| motion token | value | usage |
|---|---|---|
| ease-out | cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) | press feedback and anything entering |
| duration-press | 120ms | press feedback on buttons |

Motion answers a user action or a real state change and nothing else; the page is complete at rest. Ease-out curves, transitions rather than keyframes, no bounce; press 100-160 ms, tooltip 125-200, dropdown 150-250, modal 200-300; under reduced motion, gentler rather than off, and no content hidden at rest (FD03).

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do take every colour, size, radius, shadow and curve from these tokens through the generated CSS custom properties; never write a hex, rgb() or oklch() value in a component.
- Do put each text colour only on the grounds its pair names above; never on a gradient, an image or grain without a solid plate.
- Don't add a third type family; the monospace face is for figures, hashes and code only.
- Don't use transition: all, ease-in or a bounce on UI; use the motion tokens.
- Don't use Tailwind's default palette, arbitrary values such as bg-[#hex], or a default Geist or Inter import.
